description: Randomisation and nonparametric tests: is the absence of classical NLS motifs in Gat2 statistically meaningful?
code:
import requests, re, numpy as np, pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
rng=np.random.default_rng(0)

def fa(a): return "".join(requests.get(f"https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/{a}.fasta",timeout=60).text.strip().split("\n")[1:])
P={"ScGat2":"P40209","Cg_Gat2like":"Q6FR51","Zr_Gat2like":"C5DQ45","Ag_Gat2like":"Q759M7",
   "Kl_Gat2like":"Q6CJP0","Nc_Gat2like":"C5DI42","ScGln3":"P18494","ScGat1":"P43574",
   "ScDal80":"P26343","ScGzf3":"P42944"}
S={k:fa(v) for k,v in P.items()}
def nmono(s): return len(re.findall(r"(?=[KR][KR].[KR])",s))

# ---- Test 1: is zero classical NLS in ScGat2 surprising given its composition? ----
print("=== Composition-matched randomisation test (10,000 shuffles per protein) ===")
res=[]
for k,s in S.items():
    obs=nmono(s)
    arr=np.array(list(s))
    null=np.array([nmono("".join(rng.permutation(arr))) for _ in range(10000)])
    p_low=(null<=obs).mean(); p_high=(null>=obs).mean()
    res.append(dict(protein=k,length=len(s),pct_KR=round(100*sum(c in "KR" for c in s)/len(s),1),
                    observed=obs,null_mean=round(null.mean(),2),null_sd=round(null.std(),2),
                    p_fewer_than_expected=round(p_low,4)))
R=pd.DataFrame(res)
print(R.to_string(index=False))

# ---- Test 2: Gat2 orthologs vs NCR GATA factors, classical NLS count ----
g2=[nmono(S[k]) for k in ["ScGat2","Cg_Gat2like","Zr_Gat2like","Ag_Gat2like","Kl_Gat2like","Nc_Gat2like"]]
ncr=[nmono(S[k]) for k in ["ScGln3","ScGat1","ScDal80","ScGzf3"]]
u,p=mannwhitneyu(g2,ncr,alternative="two-sided")
print(f"\nMann-Whitney classical-NLS count, Gat2 orthologs {g2} vs NCR GATA {ncr}: U={u}, p={p:.3f}")
print("  -> underpowered (n=6 vs 4); ranges overlap; NOT a discriminating feature")

# ---- Test 3: density normalised per 100 aa ----
d2=[100*nmono(S[k])/len(S[k]) for k in ["ScGat2","Cg_Gat2like","Zr_Gat2like","Ag_Gat2like","Kl_Gat2like","Nc_Gat2like"]]
dn=[100*nmono(S[k])/len(S[k]) for k in ["ScGln3","ScGat1","ScDal80","ScGzf3"]]
u2,p2=mannwhitneyu(d2,dn,alternative="two-sided")
print(f"NLS per 100 aa: Gat2 orthologs mean={np.mean(d2):.3f}, NCR mean={np.mean(dn):.3f}, U={u2}, p={p2:.3f}")

fig,ax=plt.subplots(figsize=(9,4.5))
y=np.arange(len(R))[::-1]
ax.errorbar(R.null_mean,y,xerr=R.null_sd,fmt="o",color="#8A8F98",capsize=3,label="composition-matched null (mean +/- SD)")
cols=["#C1553B" if "Gat2" in n or "Gat2like" in n else "#2F5D8C" for n in R.protein]
ax.scatter(R.observed,y,color=cols,s=90,zorder=3,label="observed")
ax.set_yticks(y); ax.set_yticklabels(R.protein)
ax.set_xlabel("number of (K/R)(K/R)X(K/R) classical NLS matches")
ax.set_title("Observed classical-NLS motif counts sit inside the composition-matched null for every protein tested\n"
             "red = Gat2 orthologs, blue = NCR GATA factors",fontsize=10,loc="left")
ax.legend(frameon=False,fontsize=9,loc="lower right")
for sp in ("top","right"): ax.spines[sp].set_visible(False)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
